works.title: Antibodies to distinct epitopes on MPXV enveloped virion provide additive and complete protection
works.abstract: The continuing evolution of monkeypox virus (MPXV) clades capable of sustained human-to-human transmission poses an escalating global health risk, yet no effective therapy exists for poxvirus infection. Here, we investigate a panel of human monoclonal antibodies (mAbs), derived from an antibody library, which targets A35 and B6 antigens located on the extracellular enveloped virion (EV). Four high-affinity mAbs target the central groove of the A35 dimer, whereas one targets a previously unidentified epitope on the A35 protruding loop. Three other mAbs recognize distinct, previously unmapped epitopes on the multidomain B6 antigen. Those epitopes are conserved across most orthopoxviruses. A combination of an anti-A35 and an anti-B6 antibody provides additive and complete protection from both morbidity and mortality in a lethal VACV mouse model, challenging the previous assumption that targeting both the EV and mature virion (MV) forms is required for full protection. These studies uncover critical information for next-generation therapeutics and vaccines against emerging MPXV as well as other Orthopoxvirus threats.

works.title: Nuclear NAD + promotes innate immune memory by inhibiting KDM5A-dependent histone demethylation
works.abstract: Trained immunity is tightly regulated by metabolic and epigenetic reprogramming, yet how these changes are orchestrated at the chromatin level to establish long-term innate immune memory is not fully understood. Here, we show that induction of trained immunity elevates nuclear levels of nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD + ), which directly binds to KDM5A demethylase and inhibits its activity, thereby sustaining H3K4me3 (histone H3 lysine 4 trimethylation) levels and chromatin accessibility at inflammatory gene promoters to enhance “memory” responsiveness upon restimulation. Genetic deletion or pharmacological inhibition of nicotinamide phosphoribosyltransferase (NAMPT), the rate-limiting enzyme for NAD + synthesis, impaired trained immunity and associated antitumor activity. Nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) supplementation rescued defective trained immunity–mediated antitumor activity in NAMPT-deficient and aged mice. In human cancer, NAMPT expression in myeloid cells correlated with an inflammatory tumor microenvironment. Our findings identify KDM5A as a nuclear NAD + sensor that orchestrates histone methylation and chromatin accessibility required for trained immunity.

works.title: Macrophages Are Not Welcome: Potential of CCR1/CCR2 Inhibition for Cytokine Release Prevention
works.abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cells can provide cures to patients affected by certain hematologic malignancies. Cytokine release syndrome (CRS) is a major side effect of this treatment, yet its pathophysiology remains incompletely understood and selective therapeutic options are limited. In this issue, Li and colleagues identify the CCR1-CCR2 axis as a key mediator of inflammatory macrophage recruitment to sites of CAR T-cell activation, thereby contributing to CRS. In preclinical models, blockade of this axis prevented macrophage recruitment and substantially diminished CRS severity. This discovery could open a new avenue for targeted intervention against CRS, although further validation of the role of the CCR1/CCR2 axis, particularly in clinically relevant settings, is required. See related article by Li and colleagues et al., p. XX.

works.title: Cullin-g the Brakes on T-cell Persistence
works.abstract: Adoptive T-cell therapies require T cells to sustain cytotoxic function for as long as tumor persists. In this issue, two independent studies converge on a ubiquitin-dependent pathway, centered on the cullin-5 (CUL5)-RING E3 ubiquitin ligase (CRL5) complex, as an intrinsic brake on T-cell function under repetitive antigen stimulation. Genetic disruption of individual CRL5 components preserves cytotoxicity during repeated tumor challenge. Saco and colleagues demonstrate similar benefits with pharmacologic inhibition of CRL5 and related ubiquitin ligase complexes, whereas Bachl and colleagues extend the genetic benefit across multiple antigens and receptor architectures. Targeting this pathway offers a strategy to improve T-cell functional persistence and therapeutic durability. See related article by Bachl et al., p. XXX . See related article by Saco et al., p. XXX .

works.title: Priming systemic immunity against glioblastoma
Growth factor VEGF-B sustains intestinal Tfh cell stemness to restrict Taurinivorans outgrowth and microbiota-driven obesity
works.abstract: Autocrine signaling through vascular endothelial growth factor receptor-1 (VEGFR-1) reprograms T cell metabolism upon TCR stimulation. We found that mice bearing conditional deletion of Flt1 (encoding VEGFR-1) in T cells developed spontaneous obesity with advancing age. Analyses of lymphoid and metabolic tissues identified a VEGFR-1 + T follicular helper (Tfh) population in Peyer's patches and mesenteric lymph nodes. Flt1 deletion impaired Tfh fitness and reduced secretory IgA in the gut, resulting in unrestricted expansion of the pathobiont Taurinivorans . Taurinivorans overgrowth depleted host taurine, which drove obesity via suppressed adipocyte lipolysis and thermogenesis. Mechanistically, a VEGFR-1-AKT signaling axis promoted Tfh cell stemness by limiting p53-mediated senescence. This Tfh-microbiota-obesity pathway was also observed in diet-induced obese mice and in humans. Oral administration of IgA reduced Taurinivorans and alleviated adiposity, highlighting the therapeutic potential of this axis. Tfh cell senescence impairs IgA production, disrupting gut microbial homeostasis, with consequences to host metabolic disease.

Cbfβ regulates DNA looping at the Il4-Il13 loci to control their differential expression in Th2 cells
works.abstract: Th2 cells play a central role in orchestrating type 2 immune responses by producing type 2 cytokines including IL-4 and IL-13. The master transcription factor GATA3 is essential but not sufficient for type 2 cytokine production. To better define other transcription factors that regulate type 2 cytokine expression, we performed a CRISPR-Cas9 screen after preparing a retroviral library expressing sgRNAs targeting 2,394 mouse transcription factors and cofactors. The screen revealed core-binding factor beta (Cbfβ) as a specific inducer of IL-13 that simultaneously inhibited IL-4 expression. The effect of Cbfβ on IL-13 production was confirmed both in vitro and in vivo and was independent of GATA3 induction. Mechanistically, Cbfβ induced chromatin accessibility at the HS-2 site within the Il13 promoter where the Cbfβ/Runx complex bound. Hi-TrAC analysis indicated that DNA looping between HS-2 and other enhancers was reduced upon Cbfβ deletion. Overall, our results indicate that Cbfβ directly regulates IL-13 expression by binding the Il13 promoter via the Cbfβ/Runx complex and promoting enhancer-promoter interactions that facilitate Il13 transcription.

works.title: Macrophage biology and immunoregulation in health and disease
works.abstract: Macrophages are versatile immune cells that maintain tissue homeostasis and shape disease progression through continuous adaptation to the local environment. Recent advances in single-cell, spatial, and multiomics technologies have revealed extensive diversity in tissue-specific macrophage identities and their adaptation to physiological and pathological contexts. Emerging evidence indicates that macrophage behavior emerges from the coordinated integration of ontogenetic imprinting, environmental sensing, metabolic rewiring, and epigenetic remodeling. These interconnected layers collectively determine macrophage responses in inflammatory diseases, neurodegeneration, and cancer, creating both challenges and opportunities for therapeutic intervention. In this review, we provide an overview of recent mechanistic insights into the molecular circuits governing macrophage plasticity and function and discuss how this evolving framework can inform next-generation macrophage-based therapeutic strategies to restore immune homeostasis and improve disease outcomes.

works.title: Tumor-Immune Microenvironment of Early-Onset Colorectal Cancer: Implications for Immune-Based Prevention and Therapy
works.abstract: Early-onset colorectal cancer (EOCRC), typically defined as colorectal cancer diagnosed before 50 years of age, is increasing in incidence worldwide and exhibits distinctive clinical, molecular, and environmental features compared with later-onset (LOCRC) disease. However, the tumor-immune microenvironment (TiME) of EOCRC and its implications for prevention and therapy remain poorly characterized. In this review, we synthesize current evidence on the TiME of EOCRC and contrast it with that of conventional LOCRC. We first discuss global features of the EOCRC immune landscape, including innate and adaptive immune composition, functional states, and spatial organization, highlighting areas where apparent age-related differences reflect true biology versus confounding by tumor site, stage, or mismatch repair (MMR) status. We then examine immunogenomic and epigenomic determinants-such as MMR deficiency distribution, microbial mutational signatures, chromosomal instability, and age-conditioned methylation programs-that shape neoantigen landscapes, antigen presentation, and immune evasion in younger patients. Next, we review microbiome-driven immunomodulation, focusing on dysbiosis, genotoxic bacteria, and early-life and young-adult exposures as joint modifiers of mucosal immunity and tumor development. Finally, we explore how these insights inform immune-based prevention (risk stratification, screening, diet and microbiome interventions, and chemoprevention) and immunotherapy strategies, including checkpoint blockade and rational combinations in the predominant microsatellite-stable EOCRC population.

works.title: Oncogenic KRAS Suppresses IFNγ Signaling in Tumor Cells
works.abstract: In this issue, Chen and colleagues show that MHC class II expression by pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) malignant cells is a robust biomarker of both local production of IFNγ from lymphocytes and intact IFNγ signaling. RAS pathway inhibition can restore malignant cell IFNγ responsiveness in some patients, and malignant cell MHC class II expression may indicate which patients could further benefit from immunotherapy. See related article by Chen et al., p. XX .

works.title: Watch-and-Wait after Neoadjuvant PD-1 Blockade in Nonmetastatic dMMR/MSI-H Lower Rectal Cancer: A Phase 2 Trial (BASKET)
works.abstract: Neoadjuvant PD-1 blockade produces substantial tumor regression in mismatch repair-deficient or microsatellite instability-high (dMMR/MSI-H) locally advanced lower rectal cancer (LRC), but response assessment and the safety of watch-and-wait (W&W) remain uncertain. BASKET was an open-label, multicenter, single-arm, phase 2 study conducted at two Chinese centers (ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT04643041). Patients with non-metastatic dMMR/MSI-H LRC received six cycles of neoadjuvant sintilimab (200 mg every 3 weeks), followed by multimodal assessment including endoscopy, digital rectal examination, CEA, MRI, CT, and transrectal ultrasound-guided biopsy. Patients meeting protocol-defined clinical complete response (cCR) criteria entered W&W surveillance. Of 15 treated patients, 13 completed treatment and response assessment. All 13 per-protocol patients achieved cCR and entered W&W (13/13, 100%), corresponding to 13/15 (86.7%) in the intention-to-treat (ITT) population. Only 1 of 13 per-protocol patients (7.7%) achieved radiologic complete response on MRI; persistent radiographic abnormalities were adjudicated using the other response modalities. At a median follow-up of 37.7 months (range, 0.7-56.2) in the ITT population, one death occurred 0.7 months after treatment initiation, and no local recurrence or distant metastasis. The estimated 1-year disease-free and overall survival rates were both 93.3% (95% CI, 68.1%-99.8%). Among the 13 per-protocol patients no local recurrence, distant metastasis, or death was observed. No grade 3 or higher immune-related adverse events or biopsy-related complications occurred. These findings suggest that W&W may be feasible in carefully selected patients following rigorous multimodal response assessment and with close surveillance; however, the incremental value of biopsy and the oncologic equivalence of W&W to surgery remain unproven.

Alzheimer’s genetic risk factor CASS4 controls microglial focal adhesion biology and amyloidosis
works.abstract: Recent genome-wide association studies have identified numerous Alzheimer's disease (AD) risk genes enriched in microglia, including Crk-associated substrate (Cas) scaffold protein family member 4 (CASS4), which encodes the adaptor protein CASS4. Despite its strong genetic association with AD, the role of CASS4 in disease remains poorly understood. Here, we show that full-body Cass4 deletion in 5xFAD mice increases amyloid-β (Aβ) deposition, neuronal dystrophy, and cognitive deficits. Since microglia are the predominant brain-resident cells expressing Cass4, we investigated its role in microglial responses to Aβ pathology. Loss of CASS4 impaired microglial mobilization to Aβ plaques and reduced plaque compaction. Phosphoproteomic analysis of purified microglia revealed marked disruption of focal adhesion signaling following Cass4 deletion. Consistent with this, CASS4 deficiency abrogated in vivo microglial recruitment to injury and in vitro wound healing responses, two processes that are centrally orchestrated by focal adhesion biology. Together, these findings identify CASS4 as a critical regulator of microglial function and focal adhesion biology and suggest that CASS4 may represent a therapeutic target for AD.

works.title: Vanin-pantethine metabolic axis shapes dendritic cell function and affects inflammatory disorder progression
works.abstract: Aberrant activation of dendritic cells (DCs) is intricately associated with inflammatory diseases, rendering DCs an appealing therapeutic target. Metabolites are emerging as crucial regulators of DCs, yet therapeutic strategies targeting DC metabolism for inflammatory diseases remain underexplored. Our study identifies the Vanin-pantethine-cholesterol axis as a key metabolic pathway that governs DC activation-a classical APC function. We found that Vanin is upregulated in activated DCs from autoimmune patients and mice; DC-specific Vanin deficiency significantly alleviates psoriasiform inflammation in mice. Mechanistically, Vanin hydrolyzes pantethine, leading to cholesterol and lipid raft accumulation on the cell membrane and promoting DC hyperactivation. Pantethine supplementation or pharmacologically induced Vanin inhibition reduces cholesterol overload, impedes DC activation, and mitigates psoriasiform inflammation. Notably, pantethine or RR6 treatment impairs activation of patient-derived DCs, and our investigator-initiated trial shows that pantethine combination therapy relieves clinical symptoms in psoriasis patients. Collectively, these findings establish the Vanin-pantethine-cholesterol axis as a key modulator of APC function, offering a promising metabolic approach for inflammatory diseases.

works.title: Designing a tumor landscape-modifying vaccine with a unique TLR2/6 agonist for refractory pancreatic cancer
works.abstract: Abstract Failure of cancer vaccines in clinical trials has been linked to poor preclinical translatability, immunosuppressive tumor microenvironments (TMEs), suboptimal antigen delivery to antigen-presenting cells, limited human MHC antigenicity, and insufficiently safe immune adjuvants. Therefore, this study aimed to design an integrated cancer vaccine and evaluate its efficacy in a KPC orthotopic pancreatic cancer model containing the G12D mutation. A novel immune adjuvant, C-VAX, was developed from the natural Toll-like receptor 2/6 agonist UNE-C1 and covalently linked to a KRAS G12D neoantigen and WNT5a, a tumor-associated antigen upregulated in resistant tumors. This integrated vaccine enhanced CD8⁺ T-cell infiltration and reduced α-SMA expression in the TME. The therapeutic effects were further enhanced following anti–PD-1 checkpoint blockade. These findings suggest that vaccines targeting tumor antigens and resistance-associated TME components may promote an immune-responsive TME in refractory cancers.

works.title: Tertiary Lymphoid Structures in Non–Muscle-Invasive Bladder Cancer: Quality over Quantity
works.abstract: High tertiary lymphoid structure (TLS) density predicts favorable outcomes in several solid tumors but worse outcomes in bladder cancer, and the basis for this discrepancy is unclear. In this issue, Péricart and colleagues leverage en bloc resection of non-muscle-invasive bladder tumors to show that TLS accumulate without acquiring the features of productive antitumor immunity. The work reframes TLS in this setting as structures for which functional state, not abundance, dictates their contribution to tumor control. See related article by Péricart et al., p. XX.

works.title: The EMPROR’s new groove
The maternal–fetal interface is an early hematopoietic niche enriched in distinct erythro-myeloid progenitors
works.abstract: Abstract Embryonic hematopoiesis is thought to occur exclusively in the extraembryonic yolk sac before hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) arise in the aorta–gonad–mesonephros region. Here we identify a previously unrecognized hematopoietic site at the maternal–fetal interface in mice, termed MIXER (Maternally Interfaced eXtraEmbRyonic) tissue, which develops contemporaneously with the yolk sac and exhibits robust hematopoietic activity. MIXER contains abundant hematopoietic precursors, including classical CSF1R + erythro-myeloid progenitors and a unique embryonic CD4 + CSF1R − Erythro-Myeloid PRogenitOR (eEMPROR) population. Lineage-tracing experiments demonstrate that eEMPROR cells contribute to select macrophage subpopulations during fetal development, primarily in the perivascular space. Notably, early human placental villi, before HSC emergence, also harbor CD4 + nucleated erythrocytes, indicating a conserved hematopoietic role for the maternal–fetal interface. These findings establish MIXER as an anatomically distinct niche for embryonic hematopoiesis and expand the developmental map of blood cell emergence in mammals.

works.title: A CD4-lineage erythro–myeloid progenitor within the adult bone marrow defines an alternative pathway for macrophage generation
works.abstract: Tissue-resident macrophages originate from distinct developmental sources, but their adult replenishment is thought to depend exclusively on circulating monocytes. Here we identify a previously unrecognized CD4-lineage erythro-myeloid progenitor (EMPROR) in the adult bone marrow that provides an alternative pathway for macrophage generation. EMPROR cells are phenotypically and transcriptionally distinct from hematopoietic stem cells, common myeloid progenitors and monocyte precursors, lacking Csf1r and Ccr2 while expressing Cd4 and Kit. Single-cell RNA sequencing, RNA velocity analysis and lineage assays reveal macrophage, neutrophil, megakaryocytic and erythroid potential. EMPROR cells generate perivascular and tumor-associated macrophages independently of CCR2-mediated monocyte recruitment and contribute to erythroid and granulocytic lineages under inflammatory and neoplastic conditions. Transcriptomic comparisons position EMPROR cells closest to embryonic erythro-myeloid progenitors, indicating the persistence of an embryonic-like program in adult bone marrow. These findings reveal an alternative pathway of adult myelopoiesis that sustains macrophage diversity beyond the classical monocyte lineage.

works.title: Colorectal cancers with distinct metastatic potential trigger divergent early T cell responses
works.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a leading cause of mortality, with most cases refractory to immunotherapy. Distinguishing tumor-induced from steady-state mucosal T cell responses represents a critical barrier to understanding CRC immunity. Using orthotopic transplantation of CRC organoids with and without metastatic potential, combined with T cell fate-mapping, we show that nonmetastatic tumors elicit early recruitment of CD8αβ+ and CD4+ T cells with cytotoxic and Th1-like programs, whereas pro-metastatic (pro-Met) tumors induce a naïve-like, hypoactivated state. Tumor-infiltrating CD4+ T cells underwent clonal expansion, including clones recognizing microbial and dietary antigens. T cells physically interacting with tumors, identified by universal LIPSTIC, were enriched for expanded and cytotoxic clones. Fate-mapped T cells from nonmetastatic tumors suppressed tumor growth in an IFN-γ-dependent manner. Mechanistically, pro-Met tumors downregulated MHCII, and Ciita targeting in nonmetastatic organoids reduced CD4+ clonal expansion and led to tumor progression. Together, these findings define divergent early T cell trajectories associated with CRC metastasis, indicating that ineffective local immune engagement precedes metastatic dissemination.

works.title: ILC2-derived IL-9 promotes eosinophil-mediated antitumor activity
works.abstract: Innate lymphoid cells (ILCs) regulate tissue immunity, yet their roles in tumor control remain incompletely understood. Here, we combined analyses of human sequencing datasets with genetic ablation mouse models and adoptive transfer experiments to identify that glucocorticoid-induced tumor necrosis factor receptor (GITR) engagement on tumor-infiltrating group 2 ILCs (ILC2s) induced activating transcription factor 3 (ATF3) and robust interleukin-9 (IL-9) production, exceeding the modest coinduction of IL-5 and IL-13. ILC2-derived IL-9 promoted intratumoral eosinophil accumulation by enhancing survival, tissue retention, and cytotoxicity through tumor-induced IL-9 receptor expression. Eosinophil ablation abolished GITR-mediated tumor control, whereas adoptive eosinophil transfer restored it. This IL-9-eosinophil pathway suppressed tumor growth in the absence of adaptive lymphocytes. In human datasets, IL-9 and eosinophil signatures were associated with favorable prognosis in melanoma and lung adenocarcinoma. These findings define an innate pathway linking ILC2s to eosinophil-mediated tumor immunity and support GITR agonism as a therapeutic strategy.

works.title: An autonomous macrophage-nociceptor mechanosensory relay drives chronic visceral pain
works.abstract: Visceral pain in ulcerative colitis is conventionally attributed to inflammatory cascades, though whether immune cells directly transduce mechanical cues into nociceptive signals remains unclear. Here, we show that the mechanosensitive channel Piezo1 in tissue-resident CX3CR1 + macrophages directly drives colitis-associated visceral hypersensitivity. Piezo1 triggered calcium influx and nuclear factor κB nuclear translocation that occupied the Ngf promoter to induce nerve growth factor (NGF) synthesis. This macrophage-derived NGF remodeled and sensitized the peripheral terminals of TRPV1 + nociceptive afferents in neuroimmune units. Using a minimally inflammatory intracolonic zymosan model, we found that this Piezo1-NGF-TrkA axis functions as a direct mechanosensory relay largely independent of cytokine cascades. Genetic deletion of Piezo1 or Ngf in resident macrophages, or Ntrk1 in TRPV1 + neurons, abolished visceral hyperalgesia in both inflammatory and noninflammatory models. These findings reveal tissue-resident macrophages as autonomous mechanical sensors that establish a direct, parallel pain transmission pathway to sensory nerves during disease.

works.title: LM103, an Autologous Tumor-Infiltrating Lymphocyte Monotherapy, in Patients with Advanced Melanoma Resistant to Standard Therapy
works.abstract: We conducted a phase I study to evaluate the safety, clinical activity, and immune correlates of autologous tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TIL) therapy LM103 in Chinese patients with refractory metastatic melanoma. Fourteen patients with refractory metastatic melanoma received lymphodepleting chemotherapy followed by LM103 infusion (3.58-19.47×10¹⁰ cells) and high-dose interleukin-2. Characteristics of baseline tumor, TIL products and pre-/post-infusion peripheral blood were analyzed. LM103 therapy demonstrated manageable safety and promising efficacy. TEAEs included myelosuppression (100%), capillary leak syndrome (100%), fever (85.7%), and rash (71.4%). Grade 3-4 TEAEs included leukopenia (85.7%), neutropenia (78.6%), lymphopenia (78.6%), fever (71.4%), and thrombocytopenia (57.1%). The objective response rate was 35.7% (95% confidence interval [CI], 12.76 to 64.86), and the disease control rate was 85.7% (95% CI, 57.19 to 98.22). Median progression-free survival was 4.52 months (95% CI, 2.07 to 14.31), and median overall survival was 16.58 months (95% CI, 5.16 to not estimable). Baseline tumor immune infiltration and mutational burden were not associated with clinical outcome. LM103 infusion induced marked peripheral T cell receptor repertoire remodeling, with more than 60% of infused TIL clones detectable in peripheral blood at 6 months. Patients with superior clinical outcomes demonstrated greater expansion and persistence of dominant TIL clones. In addition, genes favoring T cells tumor infiltration were upregulated in TILs of patients with longer PFS. LM103 showed manageable safety and encouraging antitumor activity. Clinical benefit was associated with sustained in vivo clonal persistence and upregulated genes favoring tumor re-infiltration of infused TILs. Trial registration number CTR20233999.

works.title: Serine protease inhibitor A3 is a soluble SIRPα ligand that suppresses inflammation and antitumor immunity
Antigen-independent BCR signals limit differentiation and survival of IgM antibody-secreting cells
works.abstract: IgM contributes to early and durable humoral immunity, yet the mechanisms governing human IgM plasma cell (PC) maturation and persistence remain unknown. Here, using an ex vivo human B cell system, we found that IgM B cell receptor (BCR) signaling restricts IgM antibody-secreting cell (ASC) differentiation and survival. Using CRISPR-mediated gene disruption and pharmacologic inhibition, we show that surface BCR and its proximal signaling components, particularly SYK, suppressed induction of IRF4 and PRDM1, thereby restraining PC differentiation. Concurrently, ligand-independent BCR signaling increased basal calcium flux and apoptosis in IgM plasmablasts. Inhibition of BCR-proximal signaling also increased PC numbers and persistence after in vivo engraftment. Leveraging this mechanistic insight, we demonstrated that SYK KO in engineered PCs (ePCs) significantly improved output and in vivo durability of IgM-cetuximab-secreting ePCs. Together, these findings reveal IgM-BCR signaling as a previously unrecognized negative regulator of human IgM PC differentiation and survival and show that inhibition of BCR-proximal pathways can improve IgM-based cellular immunotherapies.

works.title: Parkinson’s at the brain border
works.abstract: Parkinson's disease is increasingly recognized as a disorder that extends beyond neurons. In this issue of JEM, Stevenson et al. (https://doi.org/10.1084/jem.20251245) highlight the functional consequence of α-synuclein aggregates at the brain border, uncovering their active role in reshaping lymphatic integrity and the neuroimmune macroenvironment.

works.title: Spatial confinement promotes germinal center diversity and tempers immunodominance
A single-cell atlas of human neutrophils reveals neutrophil heterogeneity across health and disease
works.abstract: Neutrophils, the most abundant leukocytes in human blood, have multifaceted roles in health and disease. Here we assembled a single-cell atlas of human neutrophils (SCAHN) by integrating transcriptome data from 1 million human neutrophils from 781 samples and 43 independent datasets. Using SCAHN, we identified multiple neutrophil subsets with distinct functions across tissues and robust changes in gene expression and subset proportions in infection, cancer, immune suppression and sex differences at single-cell resolution. Cross-species reference mapping of mouse and nonhuman primate neutrophils onto SCAHN revealed both conserved and species-specific features. Using 17,023 bulk blood transcriptome profiles from 40 datasets, we found that neutrophil-specific signatures predicted mortality in acutely ill patients at presentation, were associated with cancer diagnosis and survival, and correlated with metabolic dysfunction and long-term all-cause mortality. Our study highlights how neutrophil biology can improve immune risk stratification and develop effective diagnostic and therapeutic strategies. Khatri and colleagues assembled a single-cell atlas of 1 million human neutrophils based on the integration of 43 independent single-cell transcriptome datasets to define multiple neutrophil subsets with distinct functions across tissues and disease states.

works.title: IL-2-producing TFH cells sustain Treg cell homeostasis and immune tolerance in the gut
A tolerogenic function for gut TFH cells
FABP4 Couples Lipid Metabolism to PD-L1 Stabilization in Immunosuppressive Myeloid Cells
works.abstract: Abstract Metabolic dysregulation in obesity reshapes immune function, but how lipid signals drive immune suppression remains unclear. Herein, we identify a FABP4–PD-L1 axis that links lipid metabolism to immune checkpoint regulation in myeloid cells. Single-cell transcriptomics revealed a distinct FABP4high immunosuppressive splenic macrophage subset enriched under high-fat diet (HFD) conditions, characterized by impaired antigen presentation and elevated PD-L1 expression. Mechanistically, palmitic acid (PA) was shown to induce FABP4 and promote PD-L1 palmitoylation, leading to its stabilization on the cell surface independent of transcriptional regulation. FABP4 was essential for this process, which enabled PD-L1 surface stabilization, immunosuppression and mammary tumor progression. In humans, a conserved CD14intCD16⁺ monocyte population exhibited elevated FABP4–PD-L1 signaling and correlated with obesity and invasive breast cancer. These findings establish PD-L1 as a metabolically regulated protein and reveal a mechanism by which lipid excess drives immune evasion, suggesting FABP4 as a potential therapeutic target in cancer immunotherapy.

works.title: Lower airway microbiome transcriptional and metabolic activities influence responsiveness to immunotherapy in NSCLC
works.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have transformed the treatment of advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), yet a large proportion of patients do not respond. The lung microbiome is a key modulator of antitumor immunity, however, the functional contribution of active microbial communities and their interaction with host transcriptional programs in shaping ICI outcomes remain poorly defined. Here, we prospectively analyzed bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) samples from 71 NSCLC patients prior to ICI initiation. We profiled the microbiome and host transcriptome in the BAL to look for microbial and host signatures in the lower airways associated with treatment response. We found that enrichment of the lower airway microbiome with oral commensals was associated with disease progression and worse prognosis of patients treated with ICI. Metatranscriptomics-derived microbial clustering revealed distinct functional profiles. The microbial cluster enriched with oral commensals, which was only present among patients with poor response to ICI, had differential regulation of pathways involved in the metabolism of short-chain fatty acids, methane, and pyruvate. This cluster also correlated with host immune pathways including upregulation of interferon signaling, neutrophil degranulation, and mitophagy, all of which could contribute to the poor response to immunotherapy. In a preclinical murine model of lung cancer with dysbiosis, inoculating lung tumor-bearing mice with oral commensals increased intratumoral neutrophils and Th17 responses and impaired ICI efficacy. Our findings support the concept that microbial communities in the lower airways influence tumor-immune interactions via defined metabolic-immune axes.

works.title: Dysregulated AKT signaling reprograms osteosarcoma to drive selective reliance on EP300
works.abstract: Cancers depend on transcriptional control to maintain the malignant cell state. EP300 and CBP are paralogous master epigenetic enzymes that control normal and malignant transcription. Using a cancer-wide integrative chemical-genetic analysis, we demonstrate enhanced dependency on EP300, compared with CBP, in cell lines from most cancer lineages, including lethal osteosarcoma (OS). Using a selective EP300 degrader (JQAD1), we identify that a genetically defined subgroup of OS with dysregulation of the PI3K-AKT-mTOR pathway is genetically and chemically sensitive to loss of EP300. Activated AKT promotes sensitivity to JQAD1, driven by relocalization of EP300, CBP and H3K27ac to genetic subtype-enriched dependency loci. AKT inhibition combines with JQAD1 to synergistically suppress the growth of AKT-dysregulated OS cells in vitro and in orthotopic xenografts. These observations extend across >850 cancer cell lines, where synergy is predicted by elevated protein synthetic rates. These findings reveal determinants of EP300 degrader function in OS and provide a foundation for co-targeting EP300 and AKT in cancers with enhanced protein translation.

works.title: A genetically regulated SKAP2 switch modulates human T lymphocyte adhesion and migration
works.abstract: Genome-wide association studies investigating autoimmune disorders may reveal previously unrecognized regulators of immune cell functions. A Crohn's disease risk allele was associated with increased expression in T lymphocytes of the adapter protein Src kinase-associated phosphoprotein 2 (SKAP2), whose functional role in these cells is unknown. By analyzing T cells from individuals homozygous for either allelic variant or engineered to modulate SKAP2 endogenous levels, we found that SKAP2 promotes T cell adhesion while restraining migration, acting nonredundantly with its homologue SKAP1. Consistent with such functional differences, SKAP1 and SKAP2 displayed distinct activation-induced regulation as well as unique protein interactomes. Prolonged TCR activation triggered caspase-mediated SKAP2 cleavage, leading to the disassembly of its interactome and enabling a migratory program. Together, these findings identify SKAP2 as a genetically regulated modulator of T cell function whose expression and activity control the balance between adhesion and migration.

works.title: Cerebrospinal fluid and dural accumulation of α-synuclein impairs CNS clearance in Parkinson’s disease
works.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is characterized by the build-up of α-synuclein (α-syn) in the brain, where it drives neurodegeneration. Importantly, aggregated α-syn also accumulates in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) of PD patients, and while increasingly used for diagnosis, its pathological role remains poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that α-syn accumulation in central nervous system (CNS) border tissues promotes CNS clearance deficits, as observed in PD patients. We find that aggregated α-syn accumulates not only in the CSF but also in the dura mater of individuals with PD, and, using acute and chronic mouse models, show that α-syn deposition in these sites induces immune alterations in CNS borders and disrupts CNS clearance. Mechanistically, we reveal that α-syn at CNS borders elevates CSF TNF and demonstrate that both TNF and α-syn aggregates themselves impair lymphatic endothelial cell function. These findings demonstrate a pathological role for α-syn in the CNS border tissues and position meningeal immunity as a contributor to CNS clearance deficits in PD pathogenesis.

Disarming FcR-dependent neutrophil activation in MPO-ANCA glomerulonephritis
works.abstract: Using spatial profiling, Nishide et al. (https://doi.org/10.1084/jem.20260506) identified activated neutrophils in kidneys in anti-myeloperoxidase (MPO)-associated vasculitis. They developed one-armed antibodies that block pathogenic anti-MPO autoantibodies and prevent Fc receptor-mediated neutrophil activation, thereby attenuating renal injury in a passive transfer model. This nontoxic precision approach for disease treatment and flare prevention addresses a critical unmet need.

works.title: Epitope-diverse autoantibodies induce neutrophil–epithelial niches driving kidney injury in ANCA-associated glomerulonephritis
works.abstract: Autoantibody-mediated inflammation drives tissue injury in autoimmune diseases, yet how pathogenic antibodies evoke local immune activation remains poorly understood. Here, we show that spatially organized neutrophil-epithelial niches contribute to kidney injury in myeloperoxidase (MPO)-antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody-associated glomerulonephritis. Single-cell-resolved spatial transcriptomics of treatment-naïve patient kidney biopsies identified early-phase inflammatory niches enriched with HAVCR1+ injured proximal tubular epithelial cells, neutrophils, lymphocytes, and TREM2+ macrophages. Injured epithelial cells expressed chemokines including CXCL6 and CXCL16, defining a microenvironment associated with local immune cell accumulation. Neutrophils within these niches were characterized by transcriptional programs enriched for type II interferon and Fcγ receptor (FcγR)-related signaling. Mechanistically, combinations of monoclonal anti-MPO antibodies recognizing distinct epitopes enhanced neutrophil activation and induced pauci-immune crescentic glomerulonephritis in mice, recapitulating key aspects of epithelial injury observed in human kidneys. One-armed anti-MPO antibodies engineered to minimize FcγR engagement ameliorated kidney injury in mice. Together, these findings identify pathogenic neutrophil-epithelial niche formation as a driver of autoimmune kidney injury.

works.title: Dysregulated thymus-ovary axis promotes virtual memory T cell polarization to aggravate PMOS pathology
Malignant Ascites Harbors Immune Niche with IL-10 Enriched Effector Dysfunction and Persistent Cancer-Binding IgG
works.abstract: Malignant ascites provides a window into cancer-immune interactions in the peritoneal cavity. Using Cytometry by Time of Flight (CyTOF), we analyzed ascitic immune cells collected from patients with advanced gastrointestinal cancers, nonmalignant forms of hepatitis (NMH), and healthy control peripheral blood mononuclear cells (HC PBMCs). Compositionally, ascitic immune cells shared a myeloid-rich, B and naïve T cell-low signature relative to HC PBMCs. Underneath the shared ascitic compositional signature, three major functional immunophenotypes emerged in response to exogenous stimulation along a suppressive to cytotoxic axis, aligning with Luminex measurements of ascitic cytokine levels: IL-10 enriched, Nonpolarized, and Granzyme B (GZMB) enriched. In our cohort, the IL-10 enriched functional immunophenotype was exclusive to samples from patients with cancer while the GZMB enriched response was dominated by NMH samples. Ascites from patients with pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) contained a persistent anti-cancer humoral response characterized by IgG that bound to autologous ascitic PDAC cells and multiple allogeneic PDAC cell lines.

works.title: Embracing macrophage complexity for research and translation
Glycome remodeling programs pathogenic γδ T17 cell responses in autoimmunity
works.abstract: Glycans play fundamental roles in T cell biology; however, the glycome landscape of γδ T cells remains to be unlocked. Despite the growing importance of γδ T cells in host defense, tissue homeostasis, and diseases, the glycosylation mechanisms guiding their activation, commitment, and function remain poorly defined. By performing single-cell RNA sequencing, we revealed that type 3/γδ T17/interleukin-17A (IL-17A)–committed γδ T cells rely on ( N-acetylglucosaminyltransferase 1 ) MGAT1 – MGAT5 –mediated branched N-glycosylation. We further demonstrated that the absence of branched N -glycans on γδ T cells acts as a peripheral signal, driving an IL-17A–pro-inflammatory phenotype, alongside a shift to a Vγ4 + subset and the imprinting of innate-like properties. This altered glycoform of type 3 γδ T cells was shown to induce severe psoriasis. γδ T cells from patients with autoimmune and inflammatory diseases exhibited a deficiency in branched N -glycans. Glycan supplementation can reprogram γδ T cells toward a less-pathogenic state, highlighting N -glycans as a previously unrecognized immune checkpoint for γδ T cells.

works.title: STAT3 operates as an inflammation-dependent transcriptional switch in antiviral NK cells
works.abstract: The immune system integrates signals to regulate immune responses, forming complex context-dependent networks where identical cues produce distinct outcomes. Signal transducer and activator of transcription (STAT) transcription factors convert cytokine receptor engagement into transcriptional responses, serving as central regulatory hubs. How concurrent STAT activation across different environments shapes immune cell function remains unclear. Here, we show that STAT3 plays a context-dependent role in antiviral natural killer (NK) cells, either promoting or impairing adaptive responses depending on the inflammatory milieu during mouse cytomegalovirus (MCMV) infection. STAT3 is recruited to distinct genomic loci depending on IL-15 or type I interferon availability, thus driving alternative transcriptional programs. Mechanistically, STAT3 differentially regulates downstream transcription factors MYB and B lymphocyte-induced maturation protein-1 (BLIMP-1) to shape NK cell differentiation during homeostasis and infection. STAT3 relocation is governed by epigenetic mechanisms and preferred relocation toward distinct STAT motifs. Thus, STAT3 functions as a cytokine-sensing transcriptional switch integrating IL-15 and type I interferon signals to control lymphocyte adaptation during viral infection.

works.title: Glutamate attenuates the ILC2 response and allergic airway inflammation via the kainate receptor GluK2
works.abstract: Abstract Group 2 innate lymphoid cells (ILC2s) play a critical role in initiating the type 2 immune response, particularly in allergic airway diseases. Although the effects of glutamate on the immune system have been reported previously, its role in modulating the function of ILC2s and lung inflammation remains unclear. In this study, we report that the glutamate levels increased in lung tissue following exposure to allergens. Consequently, glutamate was found to restrain ILC2 responses during lung inflammation in mice. Using Rag1 −/− mice, we demonstrated that the inhibitory effect of glutamate on type 2 inflammation was independent of T and B cells. Further ILC2 adoptive transfer experiments in Rag −/− Il2rg −/− mice confirmed that glutamate likely exerted its effects by directly targeting ILC2s. In vitro experiments revealed that glutamate suppressed ILC2 function through ionic kainate receptor signaling. Genetic deletion of the kainate receptor subunit GluK2 enhanced ILC2 responses and exacerbated type 2 lung inflammation. Mechanistically, transcriptome and metabolic analyses revealed that glutamate reduced oxidative metabolism in ILC2s, thereby limiting their activation. Consistently, in vivo administration of BPAM344—a positive allosteric modulator that potentiates GluK2 signaling—effectively suppressed allergen-induced type 2 inflammation. Notably, ILC2-specific GluK2 deletion markedly attenuated the anti-inflammatory effects of BPAM344, indicating that its protective effects depend on ILC2-intrinsic GluK2 signaling. These findings demonstrate a novel role for glutamate in restraining ILC2 function, as it plays a protective role in alleviating airway inflammation. We propose that GluK2 activation may offer a promising therapeutic strategy for treating ILC2-driven allergic asthma.

Tuning T cells to give cancer the blues
Disruption of the CRL5 ubiquitin ligase complex enhances engineered T-cell persistence under chronic tumor antigen exposure
works.abstract: Engineered T-cell therapies are limited by progressive dysfunction under chronic tumor antigen exposure, and genetic perturbation of negative regulators has emerged as a promising strategy to sustain effector activity. We reanalyzed a genome-wide CRISPR knockout screen in primary human T cells under repetitive tumor stimulation; protein-protein interaction mapping revealed seven members of the Cullin-RING Ligase 5 (CRL5) complex as an enriched hit cluster. Knockout of any of these members (CUL5, ARIH2, RNF7, UBE2F, UBE2L3, CISH, DCUN1D3) enhanced tumor serial killing, and CUL5, the complex scaffold, emerged as the strongest target. CUL5 knockout T cells exhibited sustained cytotoxicity, elevated effector cytokine production, and fewer exhaustion marker-positive cells while retaining antigen specificity and cytokine dependence. Quantitative ubiquitylation proteomics in resting, and acutely and chronically stimulated T cells mapped CRL5-dependent candidate substrates beyond the canonical JAK/STAT axis, including nutrient transporters, receptor trafficking proteins, and TCR signaling components. The benefit of CUL5 knockout extended across CARs targeting CD19, BCMA, and HER2 with different costimulatory domains, and to 1XX-modified CAR and HLA-independent TCR architectures. Combining CUL5 ablation with a tumor-induced IL-2 circuit produced tumor control across nine rounds of repetitive stimulation, whereas either modification alone eventually failed. In vivo, CUL5 knockout BCMA CAR T cells were enriched in the bone marrow following repeated tumor rechallenge and exhibited enhanced ex vivo cytotoxicity after nearly 90 days in tumor-bearing mice. These findings position CUL5 perturbation as a strategy to improve T-cell persistence and the efficacy of adoptive cell therapies, potentially with engineered cytokine support.

works.title: Cullin-5–RING E3 Ligase Limits CD8+ T-cell Persistence and Effector Responses during Chronic Antigen Stimulation
works.abstract: Abstract T-cell exhaustion limits durable antitumor responses and remains a barrier to adoptive cell therapies (ACT) in solid tumors. To identify regulators of T-cell persistence, we performed genome-wide CRISPR knockout screens in primary human CD8+ T cells expressing an NY-ESO-1–specific T-cell receptor and subjected them to repeat tumor cell rechallenges. These screens revealed an enrichment of single-guide RNAs targeting components of cullin–RING E3 ubiquitin ligases, particularly cullin-5–RING E3 ligase (CRL5) assemblies comprising CUL5, RNF7, and ARIH2. Disruption of CRL5 genes in T cells preserved cytotoxic activity and enhanced cytokine production while sustaining effector-associated transcriptional programs and suppressing exhaustion-related signatures. Pharmacologic inhibition of cullin neddylation with the NEDD8-activating enzyme inhibitor MLN4924 recapitulated CRL5 loss and enhanced T-cell effector function in vitro. In a human melanoma xenograft model, ACT with CRL5-deficient T cells improved tumor control. Together, these findings identify CRL5 as a negative regulator of T-cell fitness and a potential therapeutic target to enhance ACT durability in solid tumors. Significance: The CRL5 complex negatively regulates CD8+ T-cell persistence during chronic antigen stimulation, identifying CRL5 disruption as a potential strategy to sustain T-cell effector function and improve ACT. See related commentary by Hanina and Maus, p. XX . See related article by Bachl et al., p. XX .
